descriptionHtml:
Bug B18 · P1 · known

Many dates and times follow the device clock instead of server time (UAT 3.8): 'NEW TODAY', admit date, vitals date, task done time, transcript date; with a phone two days slow a held drug is stamped two days back and the next cleanup deletes it

Tickets: TFA-92584 ready for qa (UAT 3.8); TFA-92597 ready for qa (R6); TFA-92579 AC 3/4 ready for qa (NEW TODAY); TFA-94745 ready for qa (draft restore) · counts as a QA bug: yes · found on: local

Note: Root cause known (Daniela asked for server time on 10-03); the deleted drug, missing badge and wrong draft restore are new symptoms. TC-16/S18 (UAT 3.8, one device set to the wrong date): a phone a day ahead files its bedside line in a row dated tomorrow on the shared record, and the next write from a correctly clocked device lists the lines before it twice (the transcript archive trusts the device date). Which calendar day a correct device should use when its local day and the server's UTC day differ is the open question Q9 (D10); TC-16/S25 passed otherwise. Review 2026-10-14 (TFA-92579/92584): a browser whose day is ahead writes the badge roll back to the server, and every device shows Follow-up, with the matching template and billing family (TC-01/S08, TC-20/S20a; TFA-92584 AC 8). The failing cell of TC-25/S24a is the card's NEW TODAY, which compares addedAt with the device's date (PatientCard.tsx:154-156). EFS/S28 (a)(b) restore drafts by the device date (TFA-94745); (c), an old draft put in today's box, is B13's. Review 2026-10-15 (TFA-94514): the analytics day is the device date too (pilotUsageEvents / pilotDailyRounding use localDay()): a phone 3 days ahead files its rows under its own day, and an encounter across the phone midnight is split over two days and never timed (OAT-06/S10). Re-test 2026-10-16 (TC-21/S26, 25acd727): a browser two days ahead writes the badge roll with its own future day (encTypeDay 2026-10-19) to the shared record, so the correct-clock browser shows Follow-up too.

Other cases of the same bug (counted once): TC-01/S08, TC-10/S22, TC-12/S23, TC-19/S19, TC-22/S23, TC-25/S24a, TC-02/S13b, EFS/S28, TC-16/S18, TC-06/S19, TC-06/S23, TC-21/S22, TC-25/S24b, TC-19/S23, TC-21/S26

Approach · OAT-06 Measuring How the Pilot Is Working (Usage Analytics) · S10 The per-day row through the screens: 0 / 1 / many opens, a timed encounter, a regenerate, Nursing Home notes, a second device on the wrong date and zone, an encounter across local midnight

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U6 Completing an encounter fires both timestamps (Pre-Round summary opened, note marked complete), and they aggregate per physician per day (UAT OAT-06 Test 5; UAT 3.3; TFA-94514 AC 4)
  • U7 Per physician per day: notes generated, handoffs sent, and time from Pre-Round opened to note complete are aggregated and queryable in Convex (UAT OAT-06 Test 6; TFA-94514 AC 6)
  • U13 Every AI call (pre-round summary, note generation, billing, Ask AI, photo capture, handoff) logs its total time and, separately, the time the AI provider itself took, and which model answered (UAT 3.5; UAT 3.9; TFA-94514 AC 7)
  • U14 Per-day aggregation follows the server clock: a device with a wrong date, no clock set or another time zone files its events on the same day as any other device (UAT 3.8)

Test design technique: Boundary values (boundary) — Sit right on the edge of the rule (exactly on time / a minute late, empty, longest, most) and see on which side the behavior changes.

Given Fresh physician with Hospital patients A (note-ready with a note), B (encounter dictation typed by the agent), C and D (note-ready with notes) and one Nursing Home resident; T0 and the day's rollup read at T0. Browser context 1 on the correct clock; …

When R1 Hospital (context 1): open A, leave, open A again; open B; open the resident; wait 2 minutes and Mark Encounter Complete on A; on B tap Generate, then Generate again (a regenerate). R2 Nursing Home: open the resident -> Encounter -> type a visit dictation -> Generate; …

Then R1 hospital row: preRoundSummariesOpened +2 (A, B), notesCompleted +1, encountersTimed +1, minutesPreRoundToComplete + A's minutesFromPreRoundOpened (>= 2), notesGenerated >= 1 for B; the day's average (minutesPreRoundToComplete / encountersTimed) is readable from the row. …

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): UAT OAT-06 Test 5 and 6 + TFA-94514 AC 4/AC 6, UAT 3.8, and 3.5/3.9 + AC 7 for the AI calls: post-run read of usage:_dailyForActor equals the T0 values plus the judged deltas. Judged: R1 opens +2 (one per chart opened), A timed with minutes >= 2, notesGenerated >= 1 for B; R2 nursing_home +1 after the first visit; …

Where it ran: local newspec-c (new Playwright specs); test method PW · Playwright script; lane planned in the matrix: browser agent (blocked)

S10 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/OAT-06.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Triage (2026-10-14): 0 rows.

Environment: local — main e02167f → 25acd727 (10-15/16 re-tests), local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane newspec-c.

Test method: PW · Playwright script; secondary: TIME · Time / aging (clock moved) — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on local; Source: newspec-c.

UAT item: OAT-06 Measuring How the Pilot Is Working (Usage Analytics) · Section: B · Operational Acceptance Tests · Scenario: OAT-06/S10

The per-day row through the screens: 0 / 1 / many opens, a timed encounter, a regenerate, Nursing Home notes, a second device on the wrong date and zone, an encounter across local midnight

Tickets: TFA-94514 Analytics tracking (ready for qa)

New local lane newspec-c: status failed in newspec-c/results.json → failed · product (failed · product (the lane flagged a product issue; part of it is a known gap)).

Detail:

Local Playwright spec newspec-c/an2-oat06-s10-daily.spec.ts, two tests on brand-new accounts; every model call (generateNote, refreshCourseAndBackground, extractMedicationEvents, suggestBilling, parsePreRoundNotes) answered at the Convex socket. R1/R2 (judged items of the matrix oracle, 4/4 passed; their counting questions recorded): context 1 (real clock, Asia/Tokyo, day 2026-10-15): A opened twice and B once -> hospital preRoundSummariesOpened +2; Mark Encounter Complete on A 2+ minutes after its first open (a real wait) -> note_marked_complete with minutesFromPreRoundOpened 2, notesCompleted +1, encountersTimed +1, minutesPreRoundToComplete +2 (day average 2/1 = 2 min, readable from the row); B Generate -> note_generated and notesGenerated +1; Nursing Home visit 1 Generate -> note_generated against the resident, nursing_home notesGenerated +1. Recorded (Q16): A's two opens leave one pre_round_summary_opened row; B's Regenerate adds nothing (notesGenerated stays +1). Recorded (Q17): a second same-day Nursing Home visit (Pre-Round Save Note, then 'Regenerate Note') adds its own 'Visit 2 · Oct 15' course line but notesGenerated stays +1. R3/R4 judged against UAT 3.8 (Q3 still open with Daniela), 0/2: R3: a second browser context on the same account with timezoneId Pacific/Kiritimati and the clock 3 days ahead (it was signed out on load by the clock, B33; signing in through the real form under that clock worked) opened C and marked it complete: both rows carry day 2026-10-18 (the device's date) instead of context 1's 2026-10-15 and land in their own pilotDailyRounding row for 2026-10-18. R4: a context whose clock starts at 23:58 local opened D's Pre-Round (filed under 2026-10-14), the clock moved to 00:02 and Mark Encounter Complete was filed under 2026-10-15 with no minutesFromPreRoundOpened; encountersTimed stays 0 on both days although the server clock moved only seconds (one encounter split over two day rows, untimed). Cause (code read, matches): the analytics day is the device's localDay() (src/domain/localDay.ts, convex/lib/usage.ts), the same device-clock root cause as B18. U13 (providerMs / model of generateNote and suggestBilling) not re-run: the calls are answered in the browser here; the 10-15 review cites dev readings U43 / U44 / U68.

Product issue: Nothing changes on the physician's screen, but the pilot's per-physician-per-day numbers follow each phone's own date and time zone: a phone set to another zone or the wrong date files its Pre-Round opens and completed notes under another day (a separate daily row), and an encounter opened before the phone's midnight and completed after it is split across two days and never timed, so Vikram's day totals and average Pre-Round-to-complete time are wrong (UAT 3.8).

Known gap (known): true

Evidence: 9 attached.

Dev run: skipped: not runnable on dev — not-runnable-on-dev: timed-wait, device-clock, multi-session, backend-read-admin. This local result replaces that dev entry (the scenario appears once).
